chunks: Among what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Harun ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Hannat, who said:

I, Jamil ibn Darrāj, and 'Ā'idh al-Ahmasi went out as pilgrims. On the way, 'Ā'idh would often say to us: “I have a need to ask of Abū 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, something I wish to ask him about.” So I would say to him: “Wait until we meet him.”

Then when we entered upon him, we greeted him and sat down. He turned his face toward us, initiating the speech, and said: “Whoever comes to Allah with what He has made obligatory upon him, He will not ask him about anything beyond that.”

So 'Ā'idh nudged us. Then when we rose, we said: “What was your need?” He said: “What you heard.” We said: “How was this your need?” He said: “I am a man who cannot endure standing in prayer at night, so I feared that I might be taken to account for it and thus perish.”

key_terms.افْتَرَضَ: made obligatory as a binding religious duty
key_terms.الْقِيَامَ بِاللَّيْلِ: standing in worship during the night, i.e. night prayer
key_terms.حَاجَةً: a personal matter or question one seeks to ask
key_terms.فَأَهْلِكَ: and thus be ruined or perish
key_terms.مَأْخُوذًا بِهِ: taken to account or held liable for it

ai.seo_question: Is a person sinful for not being able to perform the night prayer if he fulfills the obligatory acts?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that Imam Abū 'Abd Allah عليه السلام answered a concern before it was even asked, teaching that a servant who fulfills the obligations imposed by Allah is not held to account for what lies beyond them. It highlights the distinction between obligatory acts and recommended devotional practices such as the night prayer, offering reassurance to one who feared being blameworthy for being unable to perform it.
